title: Cross-call metering for embedding → rerank → toolchain flows with partial-failure attribution
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Users are reporting surprising token/embedding charges when a single request to the non-chat API triggers an embedding call, a reranker, and optional function/tool calls. Current accounting attributes costs inconsistently (sometimes to the upstream API key, sometimes to internal service accounts) and rate-limit buckets are not throttled correctly when downstream toolcalls are slow or errored. This ticket defines a unified metering and quota model for embedding→rerank→toolchain executions that handles partial failures, retries, streamed outputs, and preserves per-customer quota/ratelimit correctness.
background: We observed three recurring classes of bugs: 1) costs billed to 'internal-service' when rerank or toolcall errors occur mid-pipeline; 2) quota tokens consumed for downstream retries are not returned/compensated on controlled failures; 3) concurrency limits/rate-limiter tokens are not held for the wall-clock duration of long-running toolcalls, allowing ephemeral bursts that break SLOs. Customer reports and billing reconciliation dashboards (billing-dashboard#proj-embed-2026) indicate misattribution affecting a small set of high-volume customers with pipelines that chain rerankers and external tool adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Single API request must produce a single billing transaction record that references all downstream model and tool invocations with per-item cost breakdowns.
Billing should attribute charges to the initiating API key/customer in 100% of non-operator error cases; operator/internal accounts only used when explicitly routed.
On partial failure (downstream error) customer-visible invoice should reflect only successfully produced artifacts and mark failed attempts separately; no silent overcharges.
Rate-limiter tokens need to be reserved for the expected wall-clock duration of downstream toolcalls or moved to a leaky-gate model; configuration toggle behind feature flag.
All changes must include end-to-end tests and reconciliation job demonstrating <0.01% attribution drift for a synthetic traffic sample over 72 hours.
No regressions to chat endpoint metering (existing tests remain green).
Security review for data in billing records (PII avoidance) completed and approval recorded.
Migration runbook and backfill script exist and tested on staging with <10 minute outage window (if any).
design_decisions: Adopt "parent-led" transactional model: one root billing id per API request with line-items for each downstream invocation. Line-items contain model id, tokens, embedding units, and tool call wall-time costs.
Hold rate-limit tokens in a 'reservation' state tied to the root billing id for the expected duration of downstream work; reservation expires and releases automatically on failure/timeouts.

On retryable downstream failures, charge only for idempotent successful invocations; retries within configured retry budget will not charge additional embedding tokens if KV-cache/prefix reuse applies (dedupe logic).
Expose a new 'metering_context_id' in internal request headers to propagate attribution across microservices (X-RW-Metering-Context). This is internal-only and scrubbed from external logs.
Feature-flag the reservation behavior (config: billing.reservations.enabled) to gradually roll out and measure impact on concurrency/latency.
Backfill approach: generate billing line-items from request logs for last 30 days using deterministic replay; store results in billing_v2 table and compare with billing_v1 to validate.
Avoid storing raw prompts or outputs in billing tables; only store hashes and size/length metadata to satisfy privacy requirements.
implementation_plan: API layer: attach root_billing_id to incoming non-chat requests and calculate estimated reservation footprint based on configured model profiles and worst-case tool latency.

Runtime changes: instrumentation points in embedding/rerank/tool adapters to emit line-item events to the billing event stream with meter_context_id, success/failure status, and precise token/embedding counts.
Billing pipeline: build billing-aggregator v2 that consumes event stream, groups events by root_billing_id, and writes final invoice-ready line-items after event window or explicit completion signal.
Rate-limiter: implement reservation API that ties tokens to root_billing_id; integrate with existing redis-based leaky bucket and add expiration/heartbeat semantics.
Storage/migration: add billing_v2 schema and backfill script; ensure reconciliation job to detect divergence and auto-open ENG tickets for >0.1% anomalies.
Config and ops: add feature flag, rollout playbook, metrics dashboard (billing_v2_reconciliation), and enabled-by-default on dedicated/private customers after validation.
Docs & SDK: update API docs to document new header X-RW-Metering-Context and note that billing is per-request root id; add guidance for customers who compose upstream toolchains.
Telemetry: add tests that assert ticket-level attribution and create synthetic load test to simulate 10k concurrent pipelines with 20% toolcall failures.
migration_steps: Run dry-run backfill for last 7 days on staging, compare billing_v1 vs billing_v2; validate line-item counts and attribution keys.
Run reconciliation job for 72 hours and require <0.01% drift before enabling feature flag in canary region.
Enable reservation feature-flag in canary (eu-west-1) for 2 large customers and observe rate-limiter behavior for 48 hours.
Execute full 30-day backfill during low-traffic window; take billing write-only lock for 5 minutes while swapping version pointer.
Post-migration: run reconciliation scanning for 24 hours and monitor for opened anomalies; have rollback plan to revert pointer and mark disputes.
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for aggregator grouping logic with interleaved events and out-of-order arrivals.
Integration tests simulating embedding->rerank->tool calls with deterministic token counts and forced failures.
Load test: 10k pipelines/sec synthetic workload with 2 behavior modes: high-latency tools and high-failure tools.
Reconciliation test: assert <0.01% attribution drift over 72-hour replay sample.
Security tests: ensure no prompt text or output is stored in billing tables; only size metadata and SHA256 hashes are stored.
monitoring_and_alerts: billing_v2_reconciliation_drift > 0.01% -> P1 pager to billing-eng oncall
reservation_expiry_rate > 1% of reservations -> investigate potential leaks in rate-limiter release path
root_billing_id_missing_events > 0.1% of requests -> log and surface in dash; open regression if >0.5%
increase in customer-initiated disputes by >2x relative baseline -> trigger rollback playbook
rollout_plan: Canary (eu-west-1) for 48h with two pilot customers; expand to 10% of traffic for 72h if reconciliation drift <0.01% and latency impact <2%. If metrics look good, schedule full rollout during weekly maintenance with 30-minute migration window for backfill. Provide customer communications and billing FAQ for affected customers.
